supporting_evidence.summary: significant deviations in scope [all services]: emailservice_latency-90 z=7265.06 (36325.3%); emailservice_latency-50 z=1329.89 (6649.5%); emailservice_cpu z=554.14 (5951.5%); checkoutservice_latency-90 z=119.54 (756.5%)
traces for emailservice: SIGNIFICANT change; own spans self-time p50 0.21->0.27ms (1.3x), errors 0.0->0.0; inbound calls self-time p50 3.81->84.13ms (22.09x), errors 0.0->0.0

alternatives_rejected.why: Network delay alone would not raise emailservice CPU by 5951% (z=554); the CPU spike shows compute saturation, and requests queuing on a starved CPU explain the 22x inbound latency (E1, E2).

alternatives_rejected.candidate: checkoutservice: latency only downstream from emailservice
alternatives_rejected.why: checkoutservice latency-90 deviation (z=119, 756%) is far smaller than emailservice's (z=7265, 36325%), and calls into emailservice slow down 22x, so checkout is a victim waiting on email (E1, E2).

proposed_fix.description: Find and stop the CPU-consuming workload in the emailservice pod, or scale out emailservice and raise its CPU limits. Then confirm that emailservice CPU and checkoutservice p90 latency return to baseline.
